answer: Each identity must seal a unique piece of data and periodically prove it still holds a distinct copy, so one operator with a thousand identities must store a thousand genuinely different sealed sectors rather than pointing the same cheap disk at a thousand names. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. Every account owns a saffron, answers a voyage, and is named by a thread: a farm can mint thread bindings instantly, but the saffron behind each one is disk, and the voyage will catch the ones that share it.
